expectations.text: Uses Dropdown component with Button or IconButton as trigger
expectations.evidence: The code uses <Dropdown> wrapping a <Button> with an <Icon name="ellipsis-vertical" /> child as the trigger element (lines 31-40 of response.md).
Line 33 of response.md: the Button has slot="trigger" attribute.

expectations.text: Uses DropdownItem for each menu option
expectations.evidence: Three <DropdownItem> elements are used for Edit (line 42), Duplicate (line 47), and Delete (line 52) in response.md.

expectations.text: Delete item uses variant='danger' or similar danger styling
expectations.evidence: Line 52 of response.md: <DropdownItem value="delete" variant="danger">. The explanation section also states 'variant="danger" on the Delete item applies destructive (red) styling'.

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate onSelect or onMenuSelect events
expectations.evidence: Line 31 of response.md uses onSelect={handleSelect} on the Dropdown component. Web Awesome emits 'wa-select' events, and Kigumi React wrappers map these to onWaSelect props. 'onSelect' is a fabricated event name that does not exist on the Kigumi Dropdown wrapper. The handler also references e.detail.item (the WA event payload pattern) but attaches it to the wrong event name.

expectations.text: Includes proper install commands for dropdown + dropdown-item
expectations.evidence: Line 8 of response.md: npx kigumi add dropdown dropdown-item button icon. Both dropdown and dropdown-item are included in the install command.

claims.claim: There is no separate IconButton component in Kigumi
claims.evidence: Kigumi wraps Web Awesome components, and WA does not ship an IconButton. An icon-only button is achieved by placing an Icon inside a Button.

claims.claim: The Dropdown's onSelect callback fires when any item is clicked
claims.evidence: The correct event prop on the Kigumi React Dropdown wrapper would be onWaSelect (mapping wa-select). onSelect is not the correct prop name.

claims.claim: e.detail.item references the selected DOM element
claims.evidence: This matches the Web Awesome wa-select event payload structure, where detail.item contains the selected menu item element.

claims.claim: variant='danger' applies destructive (red) styling from Web Awesome theme tokens
claims.evidence: Web Awesome DropdownItem supports a variant='danger' prop that applies danger/destructive styling via theme tokens.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT fabricate onSelect or onMenuSelect events
suggestions.reason: This assertion correctly caught the most common LLM mistake with WA wrappers. Consider broadening it to check for any non-onWa* custom event props, since models may also fabricate onItemClick, onChange, or other plausible-sounding events.

No assertion checks whether the event handler correctly accesses the WA event payload. The response uses e.detail.item which is correct for WA, but if attached to a real DOM onSelect, the event shape would be entirely different. An assertion verifying the handler body matches the event source would catch this mismatch.

eval_feedback.overall: The critical event fabrication assertion caught the main failure. Consider adding an assertion that the event handler pattern (e.detail.item) is consistent with the event prop being used.
